title: CLI: supabase link return password authentication failed for user "postgres" (SQLSTATE 28P01)
body:
# Bug report

- [x] I confirm this is a bug with Supabase, not with my own application. 
- [x] I confirm I have searched the [Docs](https://docs.supabase.com), GitHub [Discussions](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions), and [Discord](https://discord.supabase.com). 

## Describe the bug
When I try to use the cli to execute `supabase link`, I get the error message: password authentication failed for user "postgres" (SQLSTATE 28P01)

Command I tried to executed:
supabase link --project-ref **********
supabase link --project-ref ********** --password ********

I copied the value listed under Reference ID in the screenshot below.
![projectsettings](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/assets/33457563/5f08d35f-b283-4549-a1e6-d8017cf5f30f)

## Expected behavior
I expect to be able to successfully link my local to my remote project.

## System information

- OS: macOS Monterey 12.1
- Version of supabase-cli: 1.68.6


## Additional context

Potentially related: My project was paused for a few months. I restored it around 2-3 days ago.

comments.author: sweatybridge
comments.body:
Another alternative you could try is by setting the db password env var. For eg. 

```bash
SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD=<pass> supabase link --project-ref <ref>
```

May be there's a special character that messed up bash. Let me know!

comments.author: RobertB4
comments.body:
@sweatybridge Thanks, setting the password worked. I tried executing supabase link without setting the password to make sure that's what the issue was, and yep it was. Appreciate the help!

The server response descriptive error message says `"Message":"password authentication failed for user \"postgres\"`

I tried setting an environment variable as I have read in the above comments using the command (NB: I am on zsh terminal on MacOs)

This time around, I am not promoted to enter a password when I use the command `pnpm supabase db push` but I still have the same error.

Please any help on this will highly be appreciated. Thanks.

comments.author: jsundy
comments.body:
This was my root cause analysis on the authentication failure:

#### Root Cause Analysis: psycopg2-binary Auth Failure with Supabase Pooler
Summary: psycopg2-binary fails SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication against Supabase's Supavisor pooler. The same credentials succeed with psycopg2 (compiled against system libpq) and with psql.

## Environment:
 - macOS (Apple Silicon)
 - Supabase session pooler (`aws-1-us-east-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432`)
 - `psycopg2-binary==2.9.11`, bundled `libpq` version `170006` (`17.0.6`)
 - Auth method: `SCRAM-SHA-256`

## Symptoms:
- FATAL: password authentication failed for user "postgres" on every connection attempt
- Error is consistent regardless of password, `sslmode`, or `gssencmode` settings
- TCP connection to the pooler succeeds (ports reachable via nc)
- Password verified correct in `pg_authid` via separate MCP connection
- Failed attempts never appear in Postgres server logs — rejection happens entirely within Supavisor before reaching Postgres

## Root Cause:
`psycopg2-binary` bundles its own `libpq` (`17.0.6`) which has an incompatibility with how Supabase's Supavisor implements the `SCRAM-SHA-256` challenge-response handshake. The bundled `libpq` fails at the auth negotiation layer in a way that is silently surfaced as a password failure by the pooler.

## Evidence:
- `psql` (Homebrew `libpq`) → connects successfully with identical credentials
- `asyncpg` (independent Postgres wire protocol implementation) → also fails, suggesting the issue may be in how both clients respond to Supavisor's specific SCRAM challenge format
- `psycopg2` compiled against Homebrew system libpq → connects successfully

## Fix:
Replace `psycopg2-binary` with `psycopg2` compiled against the system `libpq`:

```toml
# pyproject.toml — before
"psycopg2-binary>=2.9.0"

# after
"psycopg2>=2.9.0"
```

## Build with Homebrew libpq paths:
```
LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl/lib -L/opt/homebrew/opt/libpq/lib" \
CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl/include -I/opt/homebrew/opt/libpq/include" \
uv sync
```
